implemented.retirement: Release marks inactive before cleanup and retains original actual bytes, ownership, resources and lease admission through both reservation and resource destructors. Attempt both destructors, preserve first error including null, then drop actual resource record value/destroy refs, captured reservation destructor, ownership and ledger membership before returning charge. Retiring owners remain observable but cannot resize, retain, transfer or adopt. Reentrant release does not trigger fallback destruction; nested disposal drains other owners without exposing capacity of live original cleanup.
implemented.native: Keep the actual native storage lease lookup until native destruction finishes using finally. Capture successful adoption separately from current ownership so initializer failure after completed retirement does not destroy its already-adopted handle again. Capture the original lease before async initialization, release it idempotently on failure, and retain unmanaged fallback behavior.
implemented.initialization: A lease deferRelease hold preserves actual admission, storage lookup and resource records until an already-started asynchronous initializer settles. Release/dispose/endScratch immediately make the lease inactive; they cannot physically destroy its still-running producer. Multiple idempotent holds retire only after the final producer settles. Native state registered after disposal is destroyed exactly once after initialization completes. Actual initializer errors precede secondary cleanup errors; after successful initialization original cleanup null is preserved before a generated disposed-owner error. Ordinary successful initialization settles its hold without retiring active storage.
implemented.scope: This slice proves actual retirement and pending-initializer lifetime. It does not admit lease/closure/Map/Set/statistics/control bootstrap before construction, solve generic allocate identity/adoption failure backing cleanup, or complete kernel/ownKeys/backend/class/caller/font/provider/Node/production/aggregate admission. Native VM/driver/codec storage and RSS remain separate.
